title: Inventory reports
measures: How much of a commodity is held in storage, such as crude oil, fuels, natural gas or grain, and how much that changed since the last report.
whyItMatters: Stocks in storage show the balance between supply and demand. A larger-than-expected fall can point to tighter supply, and a larger-than-expected rise to weaker demand or more supply.
expectations: Forecasters estimate the change before the release, and private estimates may circulate earlier. Traders compare the official figure with those numbers.
surprises: Reports have several parts, such as crude and refined fuels, and they can point different ways. A surprise that was already hinted at by private estimates may be priced in, and the reaction can fade within minutes.
limits: A draw does not guarantee a rise, and a build does not guarantee a fall. Seasons, weather, the futures curve and wider news all matter, and futures can move sharply around the release.
